FROM FORECAST TO FULFILMENT

Stock with a plan.

Set available stock, supplier lead times, and a safety-cover target.

Order estimates cover demand during lead time plus safety-cover days. They assume no incoming orders; update the stock you expect to have available.

Stockout dates are estimated from point forecasts, with no replenishment. They are shown only within the selected forecast horizon. These are planning estimates.

TIME ORDER IS PRESERVED

Learn from the past. Test on what comes next.

The model is selected on two 28-day validation windows. The final 28 days are held back for an independent test. After evaluation, the selected model is refit on all available sales.

Calendar regression

A Ridge regression learns a trend and weekday patterns. Annual Fourier terms are enabled only when the initial training window includes a full year. The intercept is not regularised.

L2 penalty α = 3 · non-negative predictions

Weekly baseline

The final observed week repeats into the forecast. It is a useful benchmark that can win when a more complex model does not improve validation errors.

Seasonal naïve · 7-day cycle

An honest planning range

Bounds use the 80th percentile of absolute validation errors. Coverage is measured on the final test. Summed product bounds are a planning envelope, not an 80% portfolio confidence interval.

No claim of guaranteed future coverage

Bring your sales history.

Drop a CSV here or choose a file. Processing stays in this browser; your sales aren’t sent to a forecasting server.

Download sample sales CSV Up to 30,000 rows · 50 products · 8 MB

A simple, daily format

dateproductunitsunit_price
2026-10-01Product A24129
2026-10-02Product A31129
2026-10-03Product A0129
  • date, product, units are required. Unit price is optional.
  • Use YYYY-MM-DD and at least 140 continuous daily observations per product.
  • All products must share the same final date. Missing days are flagged.
  • Duplicate product/date rows are summed. Zero means known zero sales.
  • Units and prices must be non-negative. Returns need separate treatment.

REAL MODELS. REPRODUCIBLE RESULTS.

A better forecast starts
with a fair test.

Explore a fictional six-product business, bring your own daily sales, and see how a learned forecast compares with simply repeating last week.

Try it in four steps

  1. Explore the demo.

    Choose a product and a 14-, 30-, 60-, or 90-day forecast. Hover over the chart for daily values.

  2. Inspect the evidence.

    Open Model performance. Compare error against the weekly baseline and check test-period range coverage.

  3. Plan stock.

    Change stock, lead time, and safety-cover days. Review order quantities and estimated stockout dates.

  4. Bring your own sales.

    Use the sample CSV format, import continuous daily records, and export the forecasts for analysis.
